comparisons.peer_summary: AMD collaborates with industry leaders and open-source initiatives on early-stage R&D and conducts product/system R&D primarily in the United States, supplemented by engineering teams in various other countries directing specific activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose commitments to contributing to open industry standards and open-source software initiatives as part of their core strategies. Intel highlights its historic contributions to standards such as CXL, Thunderbolt, and PCI Express, along with support for Linux and Android. Similarly, AMD states it works with industry leaders on consortia for early-stage R&D and actively contributes to numerous industry open-source software initiatives across a broad range of technologies. While both emphasize open standards, Intel provides specific examples of its legacy hardware standards (CXL, Thunderbolt), whereas AMD frames its contribution more broadly around early-stage R&D collaboration and open-source software.

sentences.text: We have helped set the stage for this movement, with our historic contributions in developing standards such as CXL, Thunderbolt™, and PCI Express.
We also contributed to the design, build, and validation of open-source products in the industry such as Linux, Android, and others.

We also work with industry leaders on process technology, design tools, intellectual property, software and other industry consortia to conduct early-stage R&D. We are also actively contributing to numerous industry open-source software initiatives across a broad range of technologies.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's AI strategy is focused on three priorities: delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions, expanding ecosystem partnerships to accelerate deployments, and providing compelling user experiences via the open ROCm software platform.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and AMD both prioritize 'open' platforms in their strategies, but with different focal areas. Intel's strategy centers on delivering open software and hardware platforms based on industry-defining standards and open-source products. AMD’s AI strategy also emphasizes providing compelling user experiences via the 'open ROCm software platform' to enable broader deployment of AI hardware. The comparison is related rather than identical because Intel's open platform commitment is a general business strategy covering hardware standards and broad open-source support, while AMD's specific mention of 'open' in this context is tied to its AI software ecosystem (ROCm) to drive adoption.

sentences.text: We aim to deliver open software and hardware platforms with industry-defining standards.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.

comparisons.peer_summary: These solutions accelerate software delivery and increase code quality using agile processes, DevOps solutions, and an open-first strategy to modernize mainframe environments.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Broadcom both reference an 'open' strategy, but in distinct contexts. Intel aims to deliver open software and hardware platforms based on industry standards. Broadcom applies an 'open-first strategy' specifically to help customers modernize mainframe environments using open source and open application programming technologies. The similarity lies in the strategic adoption of open-source/open standards to enhance product viability and customer integration; the difference is that Intel's open strategy is foundational to its platform standards (CXL, etc.), while Broadcom's is a solution-specific approach for mainframe modernization.

sentences.text: We aim to deliver open software and hardware platforms with industry-defining standards.

• Application Development & Testing: These solutions enable customers to accelerate software delivery while increasing code quality through the use of our agile processes and tools, and DevOps solutions. Our open-first strategy helps customers modernize their mainframe environment through the use of open source and open application programming technologies across people, process, tooling and applications, resulting in greater synergy and alignment with their corporate IT environment.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom provides Ethernet NICs, switching, and routing products optimized for AI data centers and service provider networks, focusing on high capacity, low latency, and scalability.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom emphasize 'open, standards-based' networking solutions in data centers. Intel cites its historic contributions to developing standards such as CXL and PCI Express, which are foundational to data center interconnects. Broadcom explicitly provides 'open, standards-based Ethernet network interface card (NIC) and switching solution' to resolve connectivity bottlenecks in AI data centers. Both companies leverage open standards to address high-performance computing and data center connectivity needs, though Intel focuses on the interconnect standards themselves while Broadcom focuses on the NIC/switching products built on those concepts.

sentences.text: We have helped set the stage for this movement, with our historic contributions in developing standards such as CXL, Thunderbolt™, and PCI Express.

Our products offer an enhanced, open, standards-based Ethernet network interface card ("NIC") and switching solution to resolve connectivity bottlenecks in data centers, particularly in AI data centers where compute bandwidth and cluster sizes grow rapidly.
